Author: Juvvadi Sridevi
Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi
 Criminal Petition No.171 of 2022
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Sections 482 of Cr.P.C by the petitioner/accused No.5 seeking to quash the proceedings in SC No.25 of 2021 on the file of the learned I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda District.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The case of the complainant/respondent No.2 is that upon credible information and conducting enquiry, accused No.1 confessed that he was addicted with Ganja, as he is unable to procure the same he is purchasing the pain killer from the shop of accused No.1 without any doctor prescription.
Basing on which, the complainant lodged a case registered in Cr.No.347 of 2021 for the offences punishable under sections 420, 406 of IPC and Section 22(b), 27(a) of NDPS Act.
3. Heard M/s. M.A.K.Mukheed, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. T.Madhavi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent-State.
Despite notice, there is no representation on behalf of respondent No.2.
Perused the record.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has nothing to do with the offences alleged against him, as police have absolutely no evidence to show that accused No.1 purchased pain killer tablet from the said shop and that the petitioner is the owner of the said medical shop.

It is further submitted that the tablets (Spasmo-Proxyvon Plus) which were seized by the police from accused No.1 are neither prohibited medicine nor it creates high intoxication, and only upon the confession of the accused No.1 that such tablets create intoxication, a case was registered.

Further the police have not obtained any expert doctor opinion while seizing the medicine, whether this medicine is prohibited one or dangerous to the health and as per the scientific terms the said medicine is only pain reliever and the police registered a case under NDPS Act only to harass the petitioner.

Further the petitioner's father is owner of the mulgi where the Balaji medical shop is run, the tenant is accused No.4 and the petitioner placed the rental deed before the police, inspite of that police registered the case without any whisper that the petitioner's father is landlord and without having any absolute evidence that the petitioner runs the medical shop and no case is made out under the sections as alleged by the prosecution and prayed to allow the criminal petition.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submits that there are specific allegations against the petitioner and therefore prayed to dismiss the criminal petition.

6. On perusal of the complaint and charge sheet, it is evident that only basing on the confession of accused No.1, the police have registered a case against petitioner/accused No.5 without any evidence being placed by the prosecution.

Prima facie, there is no evidence placed by the prosecution to show that the petitioner had any nexus to the alleged crime and there is no expert doctor opinion taken with regard to the medicine, whether it is prohibited one or dangerous to the health and as per scientific terms the said medicine is only pain reliever.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that prima facie there is no independent material placed against the petitioner/accused No.5 by the prosecution with regard to the allegation that the alleged tablets have been sold by the petitioner herein from the alleged medical shop without prescription and the ingredients of the offence are not made out.
Therefore, the proceedings in SC No.25 of 2021 I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda District are liable to be set aside.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. Accordingly the criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings in SC No.25 of 2021 on the file of the learned I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda District against the petitioner/accused No.5 are quashed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Nalgonda District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

JUVVADI SRIDEVI, J Date: 11.03.2025 BV Mohammed Muzammil vs The State Of Telangana on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17367614/
